knowledge:
- key_parameters: collapse=User-specified identifier (e.g., 'geneSymbol') used in ct.simpleResult and ct.regularizeContrasts to collapse target signals and enable cross-screen comparisons ;; statistics=Character vector of statistics (e.g., 'best.q', 'best.p') used in ct.compareContrasts to evaluate replication ;; cutoffs=Numeric vector of significance thresholds corresponding to the statistics in ct.compareContrasts ;; same.dir=Logical vector indicating whether compared contrasts must change in the same direction in ct.compareContrasts ;; trim=Threshold for trimming trace reads from the unnormalized object in ct.filterReads or ct.makeQCReport ;; read.floor=Minimum count threshold for filtering low abundance cassettes in ct.filterReads ;; method=Normalization method (e.g., 'scale', 'FQ', 'slope', 'controlScale', 'controlSpline') in ct.normalizeGuides ;; RRAalphaCutoff=Alpha threshold for Robust Rank Aggregation in ct.generateResults ;; scoring=Scoring method (e.g., "combined") in ct.generateResults ;; alt.annotation=List of character vectors for reagents targeting multiple elements in ct.generateResults
- alternatives: MAGeCK=Mentioned as an alternative analytical approach for CRISPR screens, with RRA alpha comparisons provided in the package layout ;; sparrow=Used for ontological enrichment testing via ct.seas ;; ComplexHeatmap=Used for generating combination matrices and UpSet plots via ct.upSet
- when_to_use: Use when analyzing pooled high-throughput screening experiments (CRISPR/Cas9, shRNA expression cassettes) to identify target genes that influence cell viability or other phenotypes, or when comparing multiple screening contrasts (e.g., validation screens, counterscreens, or time-course interactions).
- pitfalls: Ensure the first level of the sample key factor corresponds to the "control" condition (e.g., ControlReference) ;; If ct.filterReads is used, the annotation file must be updated using ct.prepareAnnotation to exclude trimmed gRNAs ;; Linear modeling frameworks (like limma/voom) may be inaccurate in heavily distorted libraries; use ct.stackGuides to visualize library distortion ;; Ties in preranked stats can occur during GSEA, which may produce unexpected results or arbitrary ordering of tied genes.

workflows.name: single_pooled_screen
workflows.intent: Preprocess, normalize, analyze, and visualize a single pooled CRISPR/shRNA screen to identify candidate target genes.
input: ann (Annotation data.frame mapping cassettes to geneID/geneSymbol)
essential.genes (Character vector of known essential genes for validation)
workflows.stages: 1. Filter low-abundance reads using ct.filterReads ;; 2. Prepare annotation using ct.prepareAnnotation ;; 3. Normalize guide counts using ct.normalizeGuides ;; 4. Perform differential expression analysis using voom, lmFit, contrasts.fit, and eBayes from limma ;; 5. Summarize gRNA signals to target level using ct.generateResults ;; 6. Perform quality control visualizations (ct.alignmentChart, ct.rawCountDensities, ct.gRNARankByReplicate, ct.viewControls, ct.guideCDF) ;; 7. Visualize target-level results (ct.contrastBarchart, ct.topTargets, ct.stackGuides, ct.viewGuides, ct.signalSummary) ;; 8. Perform gene set enrichment analysis (ct.targetSetEnrichment, ct.ROC, ct.PRC, ct.seas) ;; 9. Generate HTML reports (ct.makeReport, ct.makeQCReport, ct.makeContrastReport)
workflows.code:
es <- ct.filterReads(es, trim = 1000, sampleKey = sk)
es <- ct.normalizeGuides(es, method = "scale", plot.it = TRUE)
vm <- voom(exprs(es), design)
fit <- lmFit(vm, design)
fit <- contrasts.fit(fit, contrasts)
fit <- eBayes(fit)
ann <- ct.prepareAnnotation(ann, fit, controls = "NoTarget")
resultsDF <- ct.generateResults( fit, annotation = ann, RRAalphaCutoff = 0.1, permutations = 1000, scoring = "combined", permutation.seed = 2 )
resultsDF <- ct.generateResults( fit, annotation = ann, RRAalphaCutoff = 0.1, permutations = 1000, scoring = "combined", alt.annotation = altann, permutation.seed = 2 )
targetResultDF <- ct.simpleResult(resultsDF)
ct.alignmentChart(aln, sk)
ct.rawCountDensities(es, sk)
ct.gRNARankByReplicate(es, sk)
ct.gRNARankByReplicate(es, sk, annotation = ann, geneSymb = "NoTarget")
ct.viewControls(es, ann, sk, normalize = FALSE)
ct.viewControls(es, ann, sk, normalize = TRUE)
ct.GCbias(es, ann, sk)
ct.GCbias(fit, ann, sk)
ct.stackGuides(es, sk, plotType = "gRNA", annotation = ann, nguides = 40)
ct.stackGuides(es, sk, plotType = "Target", annotation = ann)
ct.stackGuides(es, sk, plotType = "Target", annotation = ann, subset = names(sk)[grep('Expansion', sk)])
ct.guideCDF(es, sk, plotType = "gRNA")
ct.guideCDF(es, sk, plotType = "Target", annotation = ann)
ct.contrastBarchart(resultsDF)
ct.topTargets(fit, resultsDF, ann, targets = 10, enrich = TRUE)
ct.topTargets(fit, resultsDF, ann, targets = 10, enrich = FALSE)
ct.viewGuides("Target1633", fit, ann)
ct.gRNARankByReplicate(es, sk, annotation = ann, geneSymb = "Target1633")
ct.signalSummary(resultsDF, targets = list('TargetSetA' = c(sample(unique(resultsDF$geneSymbol), 3)), 'TargetSetB' = c(sample(unique(resultsDF$geneSymbol), 2))))
ct.targetSetEnrichment(resultsDF, essential.genes)
ROC <- ct.ROC(resultsDF, essential.genes, direction = "deplete")
PRC <- ct.PRC(resultsDF, essential.genes, direction = "deplete")
ct.seas(resultsDF, gdb = genesetdb)
genesetdb.GREAT <- sparrow::convertIdentifiers(genesetdb, from = 'geneID', to = 'geneSymbol', xref = ann)
ct.seas(resultsDF, gdb = genesetdb.GREAT)
path2report <- ct.makeReport(fit = fit, eset = es, sampleKey = sk, annotation = ann, results = resultsDF, aln = aln, outdir = ".")
path2QC <- ct.makeQCReport(es, trim = 1000, log2.ratio = 0.05, sampleKey = sk, annotation = ann, aln = aln, identifier = 'Crispr_QC_Report', lib.size = NULL )
path2Contrast <- ct.makeContrastReport(eset = es, fit = fit, sampleKey = sk, results = resultsDF, annotation = ann, comparison.id = NULL, identifier = 'Crispr_Contrast_Report')

workflows.name: advanced_contrast_comparison
workflows.intent: Compare, regularize, and integrate multiple screening contrasts to identify replicated signals, interaction effects, and common pathway enrichments.
input: resultsDF (Results data.frame from a screen contrast)
allResults (List of results data.frames from multiple contrasts)
workflows.stages: 1. Convert results data.frames to target-level simpleResult objects using ct.simpleResult ;; 2. Regularize multiple contrasts to be "in register" using ct.regularizeContrasts ;; 3. Compare contrasts and identify replicated signals using ct.compareContrasts ;; 4. Visualize contrast dynamics using ct.contrastBarchart and ct.scatter ;; 5. Analyze complex interaction effects by comparing multiple simple results ;; 6. Generate UpSet plots to visualize multi-contrast overlaps using ct.upSet ;; 7. Perform multi-contrast pathway enrichment analysis using ct.seas
workflows.code:
res <- ct.simpleResult(resultsDF, collapse = 'geneSymbol')
regularized <- ct.regularizeContrasts(dflist = list('Experiment1' = res[1:1500,], 'Experiment2' = res2[1:1900,]), collapse = 'geneSymbol')
comparison <- ct.compareContrasts(dflist = regularized, statistics = c('best.q', 'best.p'), cutoffs = c(0.5,0.05), same.dir = rep(TRUE, length(regularized)))
ct.compareContrasts(dflist = regularized, statistics = c('best.q', 'best.p'), cutoffs = c(0.5,0.05), same.dir = rep(TRUE, length(regularized)), return.stats = TRUE)
ct.contrastBarchart(regularized, background = FALSE, statistic = 'best.p')
scat <- ct.scatter(regularized, targets = 'geneSymbol', statistic = 'best.p', cutoff = 0.05)
allSimple <- ct.regularizeContrasts(allResults)
time.effect <- ct.compareContrasts(list("con" = allSimple$ControlTime, "tx" = allSimple$DeathOverTime))
mod.control <- ct.compareContrasts(list("con" = allSimple$ControlTime, "Interaction" = allSimple$Interaction), same.dir = c(TRUE, FALSE))
upset <- ct.upSet(allSimple)
sparrowList <- ct.seas(allSimple, gdb = genesetdb)
